title: A blessing before the battle
hook: the Gita is over, Arjuna has picked up his bow, and Yudhishthira takes off his armor and walks toward the enemy.
carry: ashirvad: honor your elders, even across the field

segments.voice: Yesterday Arjuna saw the universal form, everything at once, and asked for his friend's familiar face. Your line: God is everything, yet comes as a friend.

The teaching ends. Arjuna tells Krishna his confusion is gone and he will do as Krishna says. He picks up his bow. Both armies roar. And then, before a single arrow flies, Yudhishthira does something strange. He takes off his armor. He lays down his weapons. He climbs out of his chariot and walks, on foot, straight toward the enemy lines. His brothers run after him, asking where he's going. The other army starts to murmur that he's come to surrender. Session six of six: what the Gita leads into.
screen: `ARJUNA PICKS UP HIS BOW` → `YUDHISHTHIRA TAKES OFF HIS ARMOR` → `WALKING TOWARD THE ENEMY`

segments.voice: Yudhishthira walks to Bhishma, bows to him, and asks his permission to fight him, and his blessing. Bhishma is moved. In Ganguli's telling, he says that if Yudhishthira had not come to him like this, he would have cursed him with defeat. Instead he blesses him: fight, and win. Then he says something painfully honest about himself. A person is a slave to wealth, but wealth is no one's slave. I am bound to the Kauravas by their wealth. Ask me for anything except to fight on your side. So Yudhishthira asks a harder question. How can you be beaten? No one can defeat me now, Bhishma tells him, and the time of my death has not yet come. Ask me again another time. Yudhishthira goes on to his teachers, Drona and Kripa, and to his uncle Shalya, and does the same with each. And when he calls out for anyone who would choose his side, one of Dhritarashtra's own sons, Yuyutsu, crosses over. Here is something Hindu families still live by: ashirvad, the blessing of elders. Before a wedding, an exam or a journey, you bow to your elders, often touching their feet, and ask for their blessing. Being on opposite sides doesn't cancel the bond. Yudhishthira is about to fight these men, and he won't begin without honoring them. And they bless him, even Bhishma, who leads the other army. Many teachers read it this way: respect isn't the same as agreement, and it doesn't wait until you agree.
screen: `HE BOWS AND ASKS A BLESSING` · `BHISHMA: I'M BOUND BY THEIR WEALTH` · `ASK ME AGAIN ANOTHER TIME` · then, large: `ASHIRVAD: BLESSING ACROSS THE FIELD`

segments.voice: Many Hindus touch an elder's feet, or simply fold their hands, before something big. Think of an elder you're at odds with, a little or a lot. Breathing in, see their face. Breathing out, find one thing in them you honestly respect, and silently ask their blessing anyway, the way Yudhishthira did. If you pray, you can hold them in your prayer. If you don't, just let the respect stay.
Bhishma Parva. The book of the grandsire who blesses his opponent, confesses what binds him, and says: ask me again.
Your line: ashirvad: honor your elders, even across the field. A blessing given to the man who would fight him. Until tomorrow.

Yudhishthira.meaning: the eldest Pandava brother, known for his truthfulness

Kripa.meaning: one of the princes' teachers, on the Kaurava side

Shalya.meaning: the Pandavas' uncle, fighting on the Kaurava side

Yuyutsu.meaning: a son of Dhritarashtra who crosses to the Pandava side

ashirvad.meaning: a blessing, asked of elders with a bow

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli (Bhishma Parva, the section after the Gita): Yudhishthira doffs his armor and walks toward the Kauravas; brothers and Krishna follow; Kaurava soldiers think he comes in fear; Bhishma says he would have cursed him had he not come; 'man is the slave of wealth, but wealth is no one's slave'; bound by the Kauravas' wealth; asks what he wants except fighting for him; on how he can be vanquished, says no one can defeat him now and his time of death has not come, and to come again.
Yuyutsu's crossing follows Yudhishthira's call to anyone who would choose the Pandavas; confirm wording.
